corrections.why: byte re-read by a non-drafting agent: Two defects. (1) Read-once vs re-read: the 64 bytes at rdx are loaded into xmm6-xmm9 at 008325B3-008325CD, before c's slot +0x50 and slot +8 calls (slot +8 receives rdx), and those registers are what 008327B7-008327C6 store; the draft's 'the 64 bytes at rdx' reads as a load at append time. (2) Growth path omits two writes: 00832785 stores the new block as data qword +0x28 and 00832795 stores the new size as capacity dword +0x20. Also the count passed to 008410B0 is movsxd (sign-extended). Rest verified: comiss/jbe min-max (NaN skips), copy of bytes +0..+0x57 with null-slot skip, 0085E710 when non-null and owner byte set, null-slot test at 008327B5.

byte re-read by a non-drafting agent: Argument provenance: when c is null, 0083837F stores rax as returned by 00847E60 (the jmp at 0083837A skips the reload), so qword +0x88 is 00847E60's return value, or 0 when the 0x80-byte block is null; it is not the block itself as the draft reads. Same for +0xA0 (00849B30's return value, second argument qword +0xA8 re-read). The null-test claims are confirmed (byte [rax+0xDD] at 00838421 runs with rax = 0 when the block is null; qword [h] at 00838592) and also apply to the k-loop and entry n-1 word stores through h, and n wraps to 0 when m is 0xFFFF (n-1 then indexes entry -1).
